author: Ash

copy.intro: You like how Bloomingdale's carries the big luxury designers and newer contemporary labels in one store. But the nearest of its 32 stores might be a long drive, or you want to see who else stocks the same mix. These stores do. Department stores come first, then the off-price and online shops people use for the same reasons, each with a note on who it suits.

bodies.nordstrom:
Nordstrom is the closest match if you like how Bloomingdale's puts contemporary labels and designers under one roof. It does the same with women's jeans, from $20 up to $835, and Madewell's The Straight Super Stretch ($148) sits right in the middle.

Two things make it easy to buy from home. Shipping is free anywhere in the US with no minimum, and there's no time limit on returns. Sizes run from 00 to 28W, with petite and plus, so it's a good first stop if you need either.

It's also easier to find, with more than 350 locations across Nordstrom, Nordstrom Local and Nordstrom Rack. Rack is the off-price side, the same job The Outlet does for Bloomingdale's.
bodies.saks-fifth-avenue:
Saks Fifth Avenue is the pick if the luxury end of Bloomingdale's is where you spend most of your time. Luxury fashion is the whole business here, sold since 1924 from a New York flagship and stores in the big luxury markets.

That's the main difference. Bloomingdale's runs from contemporary labels up to luxury, with its own private labels in the mix, while Saks stays at the top of that range. If you mostly buy denim labels like MOTHER and AGOLDE, Shopbop or Revolve will suit you better.

Saks now belongs to Exemplar Luxury Group, the company formerly called Saks Global, alongside Neiman Marcus and Bergdorf Goodman. Its outlet website, Saks OFF 5TH, is shutting down, though some OFF 5TH stores remain open.
bodies.neiman-marcus:
Neiman Marcus is our pick if you mostly shop Bloomingdale's designer labels, because its assortment is built from the top luxury houses. It's been at it since 1907, and its fall campaign runs through Altuzarra and Dries Van Noten.

You don't need a store nearby to shop it. Besides its stores, Neiman sells online and through remote selling, and the stores include flagships like Beverly Hills and NorthPark.

It no longer runs a separate outlet of its own. Last Call, the old outlet site, now sends you to Neiman's own sale section. If outlet shopping is half the reason you like Bloomingdale's, Century 21 is the off-price designer stop on this list.
bodies.bergdorf-goodman:
Bergdorf Goodman is the New York choice for designer labels. It's been a landmark at Fifth Avenue and 57th Street since 1901, with a women's store and a men's store on Fifth Avenue.

The mix runs from leading names like Brunello Cucinelli and Michael Kors Collection to emerging designers. Outside New York, BG.com carries collections for women and men, so Manhattan isn't the only way in. Its 125th year brings anniversary exclusives from Akris and Roger Vivier.

It's a single store, where Bloomingdale's has 32. So if you'd rather try the same kind of designers somewhere closer to home, Neiman Marcus, its sister under Exemplar Luxury Group, has flagships in other cities.
bodies.macys:
Macy's is Bloomingdale's sister store and the easiest one on this list to reach, with 408 locations to Bloomingdale's 32. Both belong to Macy's, Inc., which runs Bloomingdale's as its upscale, contemporary-to-luxury store.

Macy's covers fashion, beauty and home, mixing outside brands with house labels such as Charter Club and I-N-C. Then there's Backstage, its off-price shop. More than 300 Backstage shops sit inside Macy's stores or stand on their own, so full price and markdowns can be one trip.

Check your nearest store before you plan a visit. Macy's, Inc. plans to close about 150 locations under its Bold New Chapter strategy. If yours is one of them, Nordstrom ships free across the US, so it's the easy backup.
bodies.shopbop:
Shopbop is the online pick if denim is what you buy most. Its regular-price jeans start at $78, for Free People's Breezy Denim Pull On Jeans, and MOTHER has more styles than any other label.

It's been part of Amazon since 2006, and it ships to Canada, the UK and Australia as well as the US, where shipping is free with no minimum. Sizes go from 00 to 24, with denim waists from 22 to 38.

Move quickly on returns. They're free if you drop them off within 15 days of delivery, then $10 per order up to day 30. Nordstrom's no-deadline policy is kinder if you like to think it over.
bodies.century-21:
Century 21 is the off-price stop for designer labels, at up to 65% off their list price. It's one store, at 22 Cortlandt Street in Lower Manhattan, and it's been family-owned since cousins Al and Sonny Gindi started it in 1961.

Its women's racks cover hundreds of labels, from FRAME and AGOLDE denim to Theory and Vince, and the big names run up to Gucci and Prada. New stock arrives daily in limited drops, so it rewards a regular visit more than a planned one.

It doesn't sell online. Returns happen in store within 30 days, with your receipt and a government-issued ID. If you can't get to Manhattan, Bloomingdale's own The Outlet has 25 stores coast to coast.
bodies.lord-and-taylor:
Lord & Taylor is the old Manhattan department store, founded in 1826, that now sells designer labels online only. It closed its stores in 2020. Regular-price jeans start at $234.90, for Sunflower's Wide Twist Jeans, and go past $3,000.

Gucci and Balenciaga are among its most-stocked denim labels, so it sits at the designer end of this list. Prices include import duties, which helps, because many of its partners ship from outside the US.

The fine print is strict. It delivers only to the 48 contiguous states, and returns close after 14 days, with a $24 label fee off your refund. If flexible returns matter, FWRD gives you 30 days and a free label.
bodies.dover-street-market:
Dover Street Market is for the far end of designer fashion, and it's built around Comme des Garçons. Its US e-shop runs out of DSM New York, and women's jeans start at $358, for Marc Jacobs' Wide Leg Jean.

The denim tells you what kind of store it is. The Row's Dinni Jean costs $990, and the top of the range is a pair of embroidered Versace jeans at $4,220. Past Comme des Garçons, the women's labels include Simone Rocha and Miu Miu.

It has US stores in New York and Los Angeles. Online, ground shipping is free over $125, and you get 14 days to send things back. That's half of Shopbop's 30, so decide fast.
bodies.fwrd:
FWRD is the luxury online store to try if you'd rather shop Bloomingdale's designer floor from the sofa. It belongs to Revolve Group, and its jeans run from GRLFRND's Bella Low Rise Boyfriend ($235) up to KHAITE's Danielle Straight Leg ($620) and beyond.

Think of it as Revolve's designer-side sister. Revolve is the place for AGOLDE and FRAME, while FWRD reaches from couture houses to new names. US orders ship free in two days.

Returns are easy, with 30 days for a refund or exchange and a free prepaid label on US orders. The sizes are narrower than Revolve's, though, stopping at XXL with waists up to 34. If you need bigger sizes, Revolve goes up to 4X.
bodies.revolve:
Revolve is the pick for designer denim in big waist sizes, from 24 all the way to 48 inches. It's built around labels like AGOLDE and FRAME, and the AGOLDE 90's Pinch Waist Jeans ($208) are an easy first pair.

Sizes run XXS to 4X. That's a wider range than Shopbop's or FWRD's, and it covers US 00 to 24–26. Shipping and returns are both free in the US, and it's been selling since 2003.

You get 30 days for a refund or 60 for an exchange, so it's the better bet if you often swap sizes. For pricier designer denim, FWRD is its sister site, with KHAITE and Isabel Marant on the rack.

closing.heading: How to choose
closing.body:
Start with which half of Bloomingdale's you shop. For the whole department store, Nordstrom is the nearest match and the easiest to shop from home, while Macy's is the sister store most likely to be close by. For the designer floor, Saks and Neiman Marcus are the luxury stores to check, and Bergdorf Goodman is the New York splurge.

If you'd rather buy online, Shopbop and Revolve handle designer denim, with Revolve going up to a 48 waist, and FWRD is the step up to luxury. Dover Street Market is for Comme des Garçons fans. For markdowns, Century 21 is worth a Lower Manhattan trip, and Lord & Taylor suits designer buys you won't send back.

faqs.a: Yes. Bloomingdale's belongs to Macy's, Inc., headquartered at 151 West 34th Street in New York. The same company runs Bloomingdale's The Outlet, the small Bloomie's stores and Macy's itself.
Yes. Macy's, Inc. counts 32 Bloomingdale's stores, 25 Bloomingdale's The Outlet stores and four small-format Bloomie's.
Yes, it's Macy's, Inc.'s upscale store. It runs from premium luxury designers to emerging contemporary labels and its own private labels, so big names share the floor with newer ones.
Bloomingdale's dates its debut to 1872. Its tagline is still "Like No Other Store in the World."
